title: City Council District 5
statement: Two things on my desk this week, and they're the same thing said twice: a record nobody can open, and a ladder nobody finished. The Fruitvale briefing record for the Alternative Response Initiative gets executed and published — D3 families were promised they could read their own calls, and I'm not going to be the one who explains why that document is still sitting somewhere. And I'm filing written next dates for the D5 audit of that same program and for the Baylight feasibility review, because East Oakland is already inside this program and we are not expanding our exposure to a thing whose books we can't read. On the apprenticeship pipeline — staff asked me for D5's intake and placement contribution and how it hands off to an analysis that still isn't published. I'm answering that straight, not with a slogan. East Oakland's young people got the first rung from us. The rest of the ladder gets written down and handed off with a date on it, or we say out loud in this chamber that we missed them.

payload.text: Director Vance — D5's intake-and-placement contribution to the pipeline: East Oakland's placements flow through our district intake and are counted; what I can commit to in writing is the handoff, and the handoff is the problem. D5's portion is documented on our side but the step that carries it into INIT-007's placement-gap analysis is still not published, so the analysis cannot show what East Oakland actually contributed. My ask is concrete: publish the analysis with East Oakland's intake and placement figures named as their own line, not folded into a citywide average, and give D5 and D3 a written date for the district-level breakdown. Until that record exists, I'm not signing on to anything that treats East Oakland's contribution as measured. File the date, then we'll talk about moving the pipeline.
